# UD Old Occitan CronOc

Language: [Old Occitan](/pro/index.html) (code: `pro`)<br/>
Family: IE

This treebank has been part of Universal Dependencies since the UD v2.19 release.

The following people have contributed to making this treebank part of UD: Natasha Romanova, Rayan Ziane.

## Description

This is the first version of the CronOc (Corpus of Occitan Chronicles), created as part of [BREAKTHROUGH project](https://crisco.unicaen.fr/projet-breakthrough/).

Please note that CronOc treebank is still under development. A campaign of revision and morphological annotation is underway and new material is being added to the collection.



The corpus currently contains one text, late-thirteenth-century Old Languedocian version of [_Gesta Caroli Magni as Carcassonam et ad Narbonam_](https://www.arlima.net/mp/notre_dame_de_lagrasse.html), known as [_Le Roman de Lagrasse_, or _Le roman de Philomena_](https://www.arlima.net/mp/notre_dame_de_lagrasse/oc_le_roman_de_philomena.html).

Editions:

Schneegans, Fréderic-Edouard (1898) _Gesta Karoli Magni ad Carcassonam et Narbonam. Lateinischer Text und provenzalische Übersetzung mit Einleitung_. Halle: Niemeyer (Romanische Bibliothek, 15).

﻿Simonnet, Émile Jean (1987) _Édition critique du Roman de Notre-Dame de Lagrasse_. PhD Thesis, Université de Paris IV-Sorbonne. (Simonnet's edition and translation can be consulted [here](http://emile.simonnet.free.fr/sitfen/tabsom.htm)).

For CronOc corpus, the automatic transcription of the B manuscript (London, BL, Add. 21218) from the [COMETA Corpus](https://zenodo.org/records/15300719) (Wiedner 2025) was used that was checked against the manuscript and manually segmented into sentences and tokens. Some corrections to the manuscript readings were introduced that are indicated in the MISC column (original=).

<h2>Tokenization and Word Segmentation</h2>


<ul>
<li>This corpus contains 1848 sentences, 36828 tokens and 37227 syntactic words.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>All tokens in this corpus are followed by a space.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>This corpus does not contain words with spaces.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>This corpus contains 74 types of words that contain both letters and punctuation. Examples: l', d', 'l, 'ls, .Ma., s', .I., 's, qu', c', n', .VII., .V., .C., 'n, .II., .XXX., .Ia., .iiii., 'ns, .XX., .III., 'us, .X., .CCC., .LXX., .XII., .CCCC., .LX., .DCC., 'm, .XIIII., 't, .CC., .XI., m', .D., .L., .XV., ss', .XVI., .VIII., entr', .XL., 'lh, .LXXX., .M., .VI., .XIII., Port'</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>This corpus contains 399 multi-word tokens. On average, one multi-word token consists of 2.00 syntactic words.</li>
<li>There are 7 types of multi-word tokens. Examples: del, al, dels, als, el, des, pel.</li>
</ul>

<h2>Syntax</h2>

<h3>Auxiliary Verbs and Copula</h3>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 1 lemmas as copulas (<a>cop</a>). Examples: eser.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 2 lemmas as auxiliaries (<a>aux</a>). Examples: aver, eser.</li>
<li>This corpus uses 2 lemmas as passive auxiliaries (<a>aux:pass</a>). Examples: eser, aver.</li>
</ul>

<h3>Core Arguments, Oblique Arguments and Adjuncts</h3>

Here we consider only relations between verbs (parent) and nouns or pronouns (child).
<ul>
  <li><a>nsubj</a>
    <ul>
      <li>VERB-Fin--NOUN (418)</li>
      <li>VERB-Fin--PRON (580)</li>

      <li>VERB-Part--NOUN (143)</li>

    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<ul>

<h3>Verbs with Reflexive Core Objects</h3>

<ul>
  <li>This corpus contains 2 lemmas that occur at least once with a reflexive core object (<a>obj</a> or <a>iobj</a>). Examples: faire 'us, trobar me</li>
</ul>

<h3>Relations Overview</h3>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 2 relation subtypes: <a>acl:relcl</a>, <a>aux:pass</a></li>
<li>The following 5 relation types are not used in this corpus at all: <a>clf</a>, <a>compound</a>, <a>list</a>, <a>goeswith</a>, <a>dep</a></li>
</ul>
